name: Chair Pose
hero_alt: Chair Pose, seen from the side
meta_description: Not sinking low, knees past your toes, heels lifting, back arching, arms short of overhead? Four things usually hold back Chair Pose, and an exercise for each.
og_description: Four things usually hold back Chair Pose, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
lede: Hips sitting back and down, weight in your heels, torso leaning slightly forward, arms reaching up. Here’s the rubric Posewise measures it against, and what to train when you miss.
rubric_intro: Posewise checks seven things from the side. Here’s what good looks like.

rubric.name: Knee bend
rubric.good: Sitting low, thighs sinking toward level

rubric.name: Knees
rubric.good: Over your feet, not shooting past your toes

rubric.name: Arms
rubric.good: Reaching up, in line with your ears

rubric.name: Wrists
rubric.good: Straight, in line with your forearms

rubric.name: Neck
rubric.good: Long, in line with your spine

fixes.outcome: you’ll sit lower without your knees driving forward.
fixes.why: A shallow chair, or knees shooting past the toes, usually means the legs aren’t yet strong enough to sit back.
fixes.cue: Sit your hips back and down, like sitting into a chair.

fixes.outcome: your shins can tip forward while your heels stay down.
fixes.why: Tight calves stop the shins tipping forward, which caps how low you can sit, however strong your legs are.
fixes.cue: Let your shins tip forward, weight staying in your heels.

fixes.outcome: your torso will hold a steady forward lean without your low back arching.
fixes.why: Folding far forward from the low back, or staying bolt upright, usually points to core control.
fixes.cue: Sink through your hips and lift your chest.

fixes.outcome: your arms will reach up in line with your ears.
fixes.why: When shoulder range runs out overhead, the arms stop short, the wrists bend back and the shoulders creep toward the ears.
fixes.cue: Reach your arms up in line with your ears.

cues: And one cue: keep your neck long and look ahead rather than craning up at your hands.

faq.q: Should my knees go past my toes in Chair Pose?
faq.a: Keep them roughly over your toes by sitting your hips back. If you can’t see your toes, sit back more.

faq.q: Where should my weight be in Chair Pose?
faq.a: Mostly in your heels, enough that you could lift your toes. Weight in the balls of your feet pushes your knees forward.

faq.q: Should I lean forward in Chair Pose?
faq.a: A little. Your torso tips forward as your hips sit back, with your spine long. Draw your tailbone down rather than arching your low back.

faq.q: What if my shoulders hurt with my arms overhead?
faq.a: Take your hands shoulder-width or wider, or bring them to your heart. Keep your shoulders away from your ears.

faq.q: How can I check my Chair Pose form at home?
faq.a: Film yourself from the side. Or use Posewise, an iPhone app that measures your Chair Pose with the camera, speaks corrections as you hold it, and builds a six-minute daily plan for what it finds.

llms_summary: the four things that usually hold back Chair Pose (leg strength to sit low without the knees driving forward, ankle mobility to let the shins tip forward, core control for a steady forward lean, shoulder mobility for arms overhead), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
